text:
The Grand Chamber held on 21 November 2001, by 9 votes to 8, that there was no violation of Article 6(1). It found that the UK's grant of state immunity to Kuwait in Al-Adsani's civil torture claim pursued a legitimate aim and was proportionate, because international law did not yet recognise an exception to immunity for civil claims over torture committed abroad. I don't agree with the team note that immunity overrides any competing Convention guarantee. The Court assessed the immunity as a limit on the right of access to court and tested it for legitimate aim and proportionality, and it did not treat immunity as automatically prevailing.

CONFIDENCE: 96
